Labor Model
Edit the standard that drives budgeted hours for each position
Changes here recalculate budgeted hours and variance everywhere in the app. Average rates feed the P&L cost analysis.
Unifocus Standard Reference
The standard Unifocus evaluates against — read-only, straight from their Labor Standards Report
▾
These are not editable here. They mirror Unifocus's own configuration, checked band-for-band against it, so the app and the report Eoin runs the labor meeting from can't drift apart. Switch between this and the Current Standard above using the toggle at the top of the Labor page.
Rooms · night before means a day is staffed off the occupancy of the night before it; same day means the day's own. Unifocus staffs whole shifts only, so a band's hours are trimmed down to a whole number of shifts where the two don't divide evenly (Turndown's 6-hour shift is the one place that bites).

Staffing Calculator
Project headcount and labor cost based on daily occupancy
Occupancy % by day (Sat–Fri)
How to read this table
This table shows your labor cost for the month, broken down by position.
Example — Room Attendant Budget hrs: 5,200h What the approved budget planned Actual hrs: 4,980h Regular hours worked OT hrs: 120h Overtime hours (shown separately) Rate: $18.50/hr Base hourly rate (Labor Model) Budget $: $96,200 Budget hrs × rate (5,200 × $18.50) Regular $: $92,130 Regular hours × rate (4,980 × $18.50) OT $: $3,330 OT hours × rate × 1.5 ← paid at time-and-a-half (120 × $18.50 × 1.5) Actual $: $95,460 Regular $ + OT $ (what you actually spent) Variance $: −$740 ✓ Actual $ − Budget $ Negative = under budget (good)
How staffing is calculated
Enter the projected occupancy for each day of the hotel week (Sat–Fri). Each position is staffed from the standards in your Labor Model.
Example — Room Attendant at 326 rooms/day Hours/day: 183h 326 × 56.2% (Labor Model) Staff/day: 23 183 ÷ 8h shift, rounded up Total staff-days: 161 sum of staff across all 7 days (here 23 × 7) FTEs needed: 32.2 total staff-days ÷ 5
What is an FTE? A Full-Time Equivalent is one employee who works a full schedule of 5 days a week. Because the hotel runs 7 days but each person only works 5, you need more people on the roster than you schedule on any single day — the extra cover days off, vacation and call-offs.

So you'd put 23 room attendants on the floor each day, but you need about 32 people hired to cover the whole week.
How the Time Card Check works
Paychex sometimes edits a past day's hours after you've already uploaded that day's Labor Distribution report. This tool finds those days so you know exactly which one to re-upload.
1. Upload the Weekly Time Card Report PDF. The app reads each employee's hours per day.
2. For every day it compares worked-paid hours:
    • Time Card = Total − Non-Worked (excludes vacation / Flex Time)
    • App = the Paid hours from the daily PDF you uploaded
    • Overtime is included in those totals and shown on its own in the OT columns so you can see it directly.
3. A day is flagged when the worked-paid total or the OT differs by more than 0.10h, or when no daily PDF was ever uploaded for it.
4. Press Re-upload on a flagged day — the upload box opens with that date pre-set. Pick the corrected daily PDF and the day's labor and this comparison refresh automatically.
✓ = within 0.10h  •  Amber = small change  •  Red = ≥1h change or never uploaded
